title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: In an agent, what decides which step happens next after each tool result comes back?

options.text: The model decides, using the results so far
The developer's code decides, from a fixed script
The student decides, by typing each next step
The tool decides, by choosing what runs next

items.stem: A developer writes code that always does three things in this order: call the model to pull the machine name out of the student's message, call the check_calendar tool, then call the model to write the reply. Is this a workflow or an agent, and what shows it?

Every booking request follows the same steps: check the calendar for the slot, confirm the slot with the student, then write the booking. The steps never change and the budget is small. Which design fits best?

options.text: An agent, so the model can pick each step freely
Three agents, one for each of the three steps
A fixed workflow, where code runs the steps in order
An agent with a very large step limit for safety

items.stem: Which statement about workflows is correct?

options.text: A workflow never calls a language model at any step
A workflow can call a model at steps, but code sets the order
A workflow lets the model choose which step comes next
A workflow cannot use tools such as a calendar lookup

items.stem: A fixed workflow makes exactly 3 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per request, because it loops until it decides it is done. Assume every call costs $0.002. For 1,000 requests, how much more does the agent cost than the workflow, in dollars?
A student asks why their laser-cut acrylic keeps cracking. Nobody can know ahead of time which manual pages will matter or how many lookups the answer needs. Which design fits best?

options.text: A fixed workflow that always runs exactly three manual searches
A fixed workflow that books the laser cutter before it answers
One model call with no tools, answering from its training alone
An agent that picks its own searches, with a step limit
